title: Partner Syndication Asset Catalogue — Draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc is a lightweight asset catalogue to support cloud vendor and channel syndication (AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces, cloud partner catalogs, reseller syndicates). It focuses on the copy variants, technical manifest, acceptance gates, and a small QA/ops checklist we can hand to Partner PMs and Solutions Engineers.

Audience:
- Partner PMs and Channel Ops
- Partner Solutions Engineers / Onboarding PMs
- Marketing copy lead for GTM tiles

Status and notes to reviewers:
- Draft: copy and tech requirements are rough; assume iterative reviews with Partner PM + Legal + Security.
- TODO: confirm hero image rights with Legal (Marco).
- Known unknowns: Cloud catalog metadata schemas differ by vendor; we intentionally keep fields generic then map per-vendor in a follow-up mapping table.

1) Contents of the asset catalogue (high-level)
- Tile copy variants (short/medium/long) for use in catalog tiles and search results
- One-liner security & compliance badges and required links
- Technical manifest: SKU mapping, entitlement IDs, endpoint URLs, region coverage, supported models
- Asset delivery checklist: images, screenshots, videos, support docs, datasheet PDF, pricing sheet CSV
- Acceptance gates: functional QA, security review, billing & metering test, E2E install/run smoke test
- Localization & accessibility notes
- Rollout notes (canary region + fallback policy)

2) Tile copy variants (use these as starting points; give partner copy team 3 concise options each)
- Short (14–25 chars):
  - "Low-latency LLM inference"
  - "Cost-optimized LLM serving"

- Medium (45–75 chars):
  - "High-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and cost"
  - "Run open models at scale: GPU autoscale + model versioning"

- Long (1–2 lines, 120–160 chars):
  - "Redwood Inference: a unified runtime to serve LLMs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — predictable latency, cost controls, and rollout tooling for production apps."
  - "Ship LLM features quickly with autoscaling GPU pools, KV caching, and built-in fallbacks across regions — enterprise-ready SLAs available."

Copy snippets for bullets (features & benefits) — pick 3 per tile:
- "Predictable tail latencies and autoscaling GPU pools"
- "Model-aware batching and KV caching to reduce per-token cost"
- "Private deployment options: VPC & on-premises racks"
- "Per-route observability and token-level cost breakdowns"

3) Example short product description (for catalog detail page)
- Headline: "Unified LLM inference for production"
- Summary: "Redwood Inference provides a high-performance serving runtime and orchestration layer that makes inference predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Built-in observability, rollouts, and fallbacks help product teams ship with confidence."
- Use cases bullets: "Customer support summarization; real-time chat; semantic search & reranking; embeddings pipelines."

4) Technical manifest (required fields — generic canonical form)
- service_name: Redwood Inference
- short_id: redwood-inference
- supported_models: list or comma-separated (gpt-like, llama-variants, bloom variants, flax models)
- endpoints: hosted api base url (placeholder)
- sku_prefix: RDW- (partner mapping per vendor later)
- regions_supported: list (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1)
- auth_required: API key / OAuth / IAM roles
- default_limits: tokens/sec, requests/min (placeholder)

Notes: the partner listing team will need these split into the vendor-specific field names (e.g., AWS: productCode, S3AssetId; Azure: offerId, publisherId). Mapping exercise in next doc.

5) Asset delivery checklist (what we will deliver)
- Visuals:
  - Hero image (JPG 1200x600, <500KB, PNG with transparent background optional)
  - 3 screenshots (web console: deployments, metrics, rollout page) with captions
  - 30–60s explainer video (MP4 H264, 720p)
- Copy:
  - 1-line headline, 2-line summary, 3 bullets, 1–2 customer quotes (optional)
  - Datasheet PDF (one pager) with capability matrix
- Technical assets:
  - Deployment guide (md/pdf) per deployment mode
  - Quickstart snippet (curl + SDK)
  - Pricing CSV (per-token & per-embedding columns)
- Legal/compliance:
  - SOC2 attestation link or statement
  - Data processing addendum (DPA) link

6) Acceptance gates (minimum)
- Functional QA:
  - API endpoints respond with correct schema for text generation and embeddings
  - Example requests in quickstart succeed and return tokens within expected latency envelope
- Security & privacy review:
  - Confirm KMS/HSM integrations documented for private deployments
  - Confirm no PII retained in logs by default (or document retention controls)
- Billing & metering test:
  - Simulate purchase flow (if vendor supports metered billing) and verify billing line items map to our SKU mapping
- Observability hooks:
  - Provide sample telemetry tags to be surfaced in partner console (region, model_variant, customer_id hashed)

7) Localization & accessibility notes
- Translate headline + summary + bullets into at least en, fr, de, ja for initial launch. Keep short strings to <80 chars for tile fields.
- All screenshots must have alt text. Provide a plain-text transcript for explainer video.

8) Support and escalation
- Primary SE contact: Evan Chen (evan@redwood.company)
- Partner PM: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.company)
- Support SLA: link to support portal and partner escalation flow (TBD)

9) Partner responsibilities (what partner must provide)
- Accurate metadata for their platform (pricing tiers, trial entitlements)
- Signed reseller agreement and billing connector details
- Test tenant or sandbox entitlement for our QA team

10) Red flags & unresolved questions (for follow-up)
- Billing reconciliation: who is the source of truth for usage data for metered billing? (Assume vendor logs unless otherwise negotiated)
- Legal: confirm trademark usage for "Redwood Inference" on each vendor portal (Marco to confirm)
- Performance SLOs: we have suggested targets but vendors may require explicit numeric SLO statements — draft conservative targets in mapping doc.

11) Quick mapping notes for the follow-up doc (vendor-specific)
- AWS: productCode, sku, pricingDimensionId, productUrl, AMI or container image location if required
- Azure: offerId, planId, publisherId, manifest file link
- GCP: product_id, sku_id, metered_billing object

12) Acceptance checklist (compact, to attach to PR for listing)
- [ ] Tile copy (short/medium/long) approved by marketing
- [ ] Hero + 3 screenshots delivered and captioned
- [ ] Datasheet PDF uploaded and linked
- [ ] Security: SOC2 link or statement included
- [ ] Quickstart validated in vendor sandbox
- [ ] Pricing CSV uploaded and SKU mapping confirmed
- [ ] Legal sign-off on trademark and DPA

Appendix: quick copy experiments (rough, informal)
- Experiment A (developer-first tone):
  "Run LLMs where you need them. Redwood Inference gives you predictable latency, versioned rollouts, and cost controls so teams ship faster."

- Experiment B (enterprise tone):
  "Production-grade LLM inference with enterprise SLAs, private deployment options, and audit-ready observability."

- Quick A/B test idea: swap headline "Run LLMs where you need them" vs "Production-grade LLM inference" and measure tile CTR in sandbox listing.

Notes-to-self for next steps:
- Split this canonical catalogue into vendor mapping spreadsheet (assign to Sara)
- Finalize pricing CSV with Finance (Evan to schedule)
- Lock hero image assets with Legal before sending to partner portal

End of draft.

Comments and inline edits welcome — leave suggestions as comments in Confluence copy or ping in slack:#partnersync.
